assessment.rationale: Strong envelope/payload separation makes this a good fit for envelope-independence pressure: meaning lives under the pcid-selected payload handler, unknown envelopes stay opaque, and the spec explicitly avoids declaring a canonical winner. It is not a full pass because it does not define how a CAS-backed group session proves semantic equivalence across different outer-envelope bytes, and unsigned v0 pushes integrity and accountability into other layers.
strengths: Meaning is explicitly owned by the pcid-selected payload protocol rather than the outer envelope.
Unknown-pCID handling preserves exact bytes and fails explicitly without speculative parsing.
The spec explicitly rejects a central registry and avoids treating this variant as the winner.
weaknesses: No explicit rule shows how the same group-session message stays identical across different envelope variants.
Unsigned v0 weakens provenance and peer-local accountability at the envelope layer.
Canonical hashing of exact envelope bytes can still couple identifiers to the chosen wrapper.
risks: Upper layers may accidentally content-address the outer DAG-CBOR envelope, reintroducing envelope dependence.
Transport-supplied authorship could become a de facto authority or vary between deployments.
Peers may be able to store and forward opaque bytes yet still lack enough evidence to audit payload meaning.
open_questions: What should a CAS-backed session bind to when two envelope variants carry the same resolved payload?
How should peers compare or deduplicate semantically equivalent cross-variant messages using only local evidence?
Is the layering note about signature slots meant to rely on wrappers or successor variants despite the base [pcid, payload] shape?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
